verdict.line: You win this by poking him down from outside his 700-range Leap Strike and punishing his dives with R once you hit 6; you lose it if you trade autos into his E or let fights drag long enough for his attack-speed passive to take over.

brief.thesis: Jax's E (Counter Strike) only dodges basic attacks, not spells, so your Q (Boomerang Throw) keeps landing and slowing him through it even while your autos whiff for free. The whole lane is about staying outside his 700-range Q (Leap Strike), chipping him down with Boulder Toss, and making sure every fight you take is short before his R (Relentless Assault) attack-speed stacking turns it into a skirmish he wins.

theirWindow.when: Jax leaps in with Q then W
theirWindow.what: Leap Strike closes the 700-range gap and Empower (W) adds bonus damage to the hit that follows; if Counter Strike (E) is up when he lands, stop autoattacking him in melee since the stun that follows chunks you, but keep throwing Q since it still connects and slows through the dodge.

yourWindow.when: right after he burns Counter Strike (E)
yourWindow.what: E locks out basic attacks for 18/16/14/12/10s depending on rank — once it's spent, step into auto range freely, or Hop (E) onto him and Q at point-blank for full slow and damage before he can threaten a stun again.

start.why: 50.9% WR over 114 games at 57.3% pick — the extra AD speeds up your poke damage and the potion covers sustain against his auto-reliant trades.

boots.why: 51.5% WR over 163 games at 84% pick — his whole kit (autos, R passive attack speed, empowered W hits) is physical, so flat armor blunts every trade he gets.

core.why: first item in the dominant build path (57.7% WR, 26.5% pick) — the move speed and burst let you actually catch him once Rage maxes you into Mega Gnar.

runes.keystoneWhy: 52.9% WR at 34.5% pick — the heal and move speed on cast keep you topped up while you kite outside his Leap Strike range; master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo (46.5% WR, 21.2% pick) if they'd rather stand and win the attack-speed race than disengage.

summoners.why: 65.5% pick at 52.6% WR — Teleport refills your Doran's Blade and potion trips so you never cede lane tempo while out-ranging him; take Flash+Ignite (51.5% WR, 16.3% pick) instead if you want to punish a failed all-in with a kill at level 6.

playing.title: Poke from max Q range
playing.detail: Stay outside his 700-range Leap Strike and throw Boomerang Throw (Q) on cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) — it slows on hit and punishes him for standing in it.

playing.title: Ignore autos into his E
playing.detail: Counter Strike (E) dodges basic attacks only, so stop autoattacking the instant he pops it, but keep landing Q since it's a spell and still connects and slows.

playing.title: Track your own Rage meter
playing.detail: Your passive fills in combat and forces a transform into Mega Gnar at max — know whether you're about to go melee-tanky or stay ranged before you commit to a trade.

playing.title: Save R for his dive
playing.detail: At level 6+, hold GNAR! (R) for the moment he closes with Q then W — the throw slows him and stuns outright if it drives him into a wall, matching OP.GG's own read on this matchup.

playing.title: Bounce off him with E
playing.detail: Hop (E, 475 range) lets you leap onto his head and keep moving — use it to reposition and disengage the instant his E (Counter Strike) comes back up.

playing.title: Cut fights short past level 9
playing.detail: Relentless Assault (R) has no cooldown and ramps attack speed the longer a fight runs, with every third hit dealing bonus damage — commit to quick poke trades, not standing skirmishes, once he's past level 9.

playing.title: Punish failed Leap Strikes
playing.detail: He has no sustain tool beyond autos, so answering a whiffed engage with your own range swings lane tempo back in your favor immediately.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner picks are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reads on cooldowns, ranges, and trade windows are my own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Use your third basic attack on [W] and [E] to kite him. After reaching level 6, try to use [R] when he closes in to try to kill him.
